parsed.summary: The formal statements say four things about R_k(3), defined as the least n such that every k-colouring of the edges of K_n has a monochromatic triangle. (i) R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞. (ii) For every k ≥ 2, R_k(3) ≥ (c·k^{1/3}/log k)^k with the explicit constant c = 1/(6e^{38}). (iii) For each ε > 0, eventually (1/3−ε)k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε)k log k. (iv) log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k). These faithfully capture Theorem 1.1 and its corollaries; the main caveat is that the Shannon-capacity reformulation is not formalized.

glossary.plain: A k-colouring C of the edges of K_n (on Fin n) in which no colour class contains a triangle (3-clique).
Every k-colouring of E(K_n) contains a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.note: For k = 0 and n ≥ 2 no colouring exists, so the condition holds vacuously. This only affects k = 0.

glossary.plain: R_k(3) = least n such that every k-colouring of K_n has a monochromatic triangle (sInf of that set).
glossary.note: The set is nonempty for every k by Ramsey's theorem, so the sInf ∅ = 0 junk value is not triggered. The k = 0 value is 2, a convention irrelevant to asymptotics.

lean_claims.plain: For every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large k: (1/3−ε)·k·log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε)·k·log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞.

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute c > 0 such that R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for all integers k ≥ 2.
The Shannon capacity of graphs with independence number 2 is unbounded.

coverage.why: Lean fixes an explicit constant c = 1/(6e^{38}) rather than asserting that some c exists.
Taking logs, the ε-eventually formulation is exactly k^{(1/3−o(1))k} ≤ R_k ≤ k^{(1+o(1))k}.
R_k = k^{Θ(k)} means log R_k = Θ(k log k).
Direct statement that R_k^{1/k} tends to atTop.
No Shannon capacity statement appears in the Lean file.

flags.explanation: The Shannon-capacity consequence (unbounded capacity of graphs with α = 2) is not formalized.
Lean asserts the bound with the specific constant c = 1/(6e^{38}), which is stronger than the paper's existential c. This is fine.
For k = 0 there is no colouring with 0 colours once n ≥ 2, so R_0 = 2 under this definition. The value is conventional and irrelevant to every asymptotic claim and to the k ≥ 2 bound.
